newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says Maxus may share 18.44 pct gross revs.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says Maxus may share 18.44 pct gross revs.

text.p: Talks between the Ecuadorean government and U.S. oil firm Maxus Energy Corp are in their final stages and the firm is near agreeing to share 18.44 percent of revenues, a state oil firm spokesman said Friday.
"There is already an agreement on the fundamentals," the Petroecuador official told Reuters.

"We hope that the (contract) signings will take place at the end of next week," he said, adding that under the terms of the new agreement Maxus would hand over 18.44 percent of its gross revenues to the state.
"But we will still have to wait for both parties to sign," he said.
Ecuador's government August 20 banned Maxus from continuing its oil operations in the country until the firm reached an agreement to share output with Petroecuador.
Maxus, which is owned by Argentine oil firm YPF SA, normally produces 33,000 barrels a day in Ecuador.
Government sources said that the new contract with the government would be signed by the parent company YPF, and not Maxus.
Ecuadorean law specifies that foreign oil companies should in principle pay 12.5 percent of production to the state.
